meta.usage: One manifest per R<density><requirement> real-window family instance. Frozen BEFORE generation (ticket acceptance item 5). Every field under 'preregistration' is a design decision; editing it after a scenario has been generated is a prereg violation, exactly as for the M-family template.
meta.differs_from: scenario_manifest_template.json -- the M-family template's 300 s box retires here. Window width is a physical quantity computed from real orbit geometry, so there is no interval_width placeholder and no PASS_HORIZON.
meta.platform_orbit_is_required: The orbit is an input, not a default. generate_real_scenario raises rather than inventing one, so this template registers the orbit's provenance and the caller must supply matching elements.

scenario.window_semantics: real-orbit three-leg cascade: incidence mask n mode squint envelope n end-check

preregistration.cluster_assignment_rule: target i -> centre i % 8 (fixed order, no shuffle)

platform_orbit.provenance: design geometry: h=570 km, i=45 deg (platform_kim2021.json)
platform_orbit.note: supplied by the caller; the generator refuses to invent one

squint_semantics.t_ca_s: the ZERO of sss_core.geometry.squint_at -- drives the dwell closure and the AASR bandwidth
squint_semantics.vector_squint_min_t_s: the minimum of the forked VECTOR squint (realwindows.satellite_to_target_vector) -- the point the incidence mask is evaluated at
squint_semantics.why_two: These are different physical quantities with different zero points, measured: the vector minimum sits ~600 s away from the planar zero, and at closest approach they read 12.749 deg vs 0.000 deg on the same target. The mode-envelope leg consumes ONLY squint_at; the vector squint never enters an envelope test.

per_task_geometry_fields.r0_m: slant range at this task's incidence (look_geometry Eq.2-3)
per_task_geometry_fields.incidence_deg: incidence angle at the window centre
per_task_geometry_fields.vector_squint_min_t_s: vector-squint minimum within the incidence leg
per_task_geometry_fields.window_width_s: cascade width, a physical quantity in the M family
